title: Bounded northern and central European Latin missal book states

traditions.label: Nidaros provincial missal
traditions.scope: The printed 1519 Nidaros-use missal commissioned for the metropolitan province; Iceland and the Faroes are within the stated intended territory.
traditions.coverage_note: The edited print and its foreword establish the book and intended scope, but do not establish uniform local reception or a collated transition from earlier Nidaros books.

traditions.label: Turku diocesan Missale Aboense
traditions.scope: The 1488 Lübeck-printed Missale Aboense and its diocesan preface and calendar.
traditions.coverage_note: The National Library describes a composite parchment copy; print date and local components are identified, but original leaves and other copies are uncollated.

traditions.label: Zagreb diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Venetian 1511 Missale Zagrabiense bearing a title that reports diocesan synod and chapter approval under Bishop Luke.
traditions.coverage_note: The title and contents are transcribed in a scholarly catalogue. The original synod act, exact effective date, and later Zagreb cathedral and Jesuit routes are unresolved.

traditions.label: Roman-Bohemian missal
traditions.scope: The 1690 Roman-based missal printed at the Prague archiepiscopal seminary with Bohemian saints' proper Masses named on its title.
traditions.coverage_note: A digitized-book title transcription identifies the edition. Papal concession documents, original title image, complete propers, and reception remain uninspected. This is not assigned as a successor to the medieval Prague-use core.

sources.title: Missale Nidrosiense, edited transcription and introduction, Bokselskap
sources.inspection: The edited opening title, printer's foreword and calendar, with the companion introduction's content survey and colophon report, were read on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: A modern edited transcription, not an independent collation of the original print or its surviving copies; the transcription itself does not establish province-wide actual use.

sources.title: Espen Karlsen and Sigurd Hareide, The Nidaros Missal (1519)
sources.inspection: Introduction sections on commissioning, print completion, province, contents and final colophon inspected on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The account distinguishes intent from reception and notes rites absent from the missal; it is not a complete before-and-after liturgical collation.

sources.title: National Library of Finland, Missale Aboense (parchment composite) catalogue
sources.inspection: Holding-library record read on 2026-10-20, especially imprint, local preface and calendar description, composite-copy warning, and dated Bitz preface.
sources.limitations: The linked 330 MB original-image PDF was not acquired; exact leaf readings, the physical completeness of copies, and their relation to Dominican material remain unverified.

sources.title: Usuarium, Missale Zagrabiense, Book 92
sources.inspection: Catalogue title, 1511 date, OSZK shelfmark, and contents entries for calendar, Mass cycles, ordinary, Canon and rubrics inspected on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The linked original-book PDF returned 401 in this research session. Synod and chapter approval are claims in the transcribed title; the original act, adoption and source-text differences were not checked.

sources.title: Missale Romano-Bohemicum (Prague, 1690), digitized-book title listing
sources.inspection: Long title and 1690 archiepiscopal-seminary imprint read from the digitized-book listing on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The original title image and body were not inspected; title language concerning pontifical concessions and the archbishop's mandate is not the underlying acts or local use evidence.

sources.title: National Library of Finland, Missale Aboense parchment composite, Doria PDF fv31282_pergamenttikooste.pdf
sources.inspection: Whole 540-page PDF (330,077,146 bytes) acquired 2026-10-21; pp. 1–24 surveyed and pp. 6 (computus table), 7 (January), 12 (June), 18 (December) and 19 (holy-water ordo) viewed.
sources.limitations: A composite of leaves from several copies; the Bitz preface leaf was not found in pp. 1–24. Only selected calendar months were read.

stages.label: Printed Nidaros provincial missal
stages.scope: Printed Mass book's foreword, calendar, temporal, Order and Canon of Mass, sanctoral, commons, votives, sequences and accident rubrics as bounded by the edited copy's contents.
stages.summary: Archbishop Erik Valkendorf commissioned a corrected and augmented missal following the Nidaros metropolitan rite because older missals were scarce or defective. The print foreword states a goal of common celebration across his diocese and province; the edited colophon dates printing to 25 May 1519.

evidence.locus: part 1, opening title and printer's foreword, numbered paragraphs 1–2
evidence.claim: The book names Nidaros use, Archbishop Valkendorf's commission and a province-wide standardization intention.

evidence.locus: The Nidaros missal, first book printed on Norwegian initiative, paragraphs 3–5; content section, contents through colophon
evidence.claim: The authors identify the 25 May 1519 print completion and bounded missal components, including an Order/Canon, propers, calendar and rubrics.

stages.limitations: The original print and pre-1519 witnesses have not been collated against the edited transcription; no exact new prayer or rubric is identified here. The missal excludes some processions and blessings supplied by other Nidaros books.
stages.reception: The source establishes provincial intent, including Iceland and the Faroes, but no local adoption date or uniform observance there.

stages.label: Turku diocesan Missale Aboense
stages.date_label: 1488 printing after the 17 August bishop's preface
stages.scope: Local preface and saints' calendar in a diocesan missal printed at Lübeck; only the calendar is counted as a demonstrated local liturgical component.
stages.witness_label: Missale Aboense, 1488 print represented by the National Library parchment composite
stages.summary: The National Library identifies the Lübeck 1488 Missale Aboense for the Diocese of Turku, with Bishop Konrad Bitz's preface dated 17 August 1488 and a local saints' calendar. The surviving parchment object is assembled from fragments of multiple copies.

evidence.locus: Finna record, imprint and description paragraphs beginning 'MISSALE ABOENSE' and 'Esipuhe ja alkuun liitetty'
evidence.claim: Identifies the diocesan destination, 1488 Lübeck print, dated bishop's preface, and Finnish local calendar.

evidence.locus: Doria PDF pp. 7, 12 and 18 (January, June, December calendar)
evidence.claim: The printed calendar marks Henry bishop (20 January) and the Translation of Henry (18 June) as totum duplex, with Knut king (7 January), Eskil martyr (12 June), a church dedication (17 June) and Anne mother of Mary (9 December) as local entries.

stages.limitations: 17 August is a prefatory date, not the print or use date. Only the January, June and December calendar pages were read in the composite copy; other Mass components are uncollated. Fragmentary and composite copies cannot be treated as a single physically complete witness.
stages.reception: The book's intended Turku diocesan destination is documented by the holding library; individual parish use is not dated.

stages.label: 1511 Zagreb diocesan missal
stages.scope: Catalogue-attested diocesan missal with calendar, temporal and sanctoral Masses, ordinary, Canon and rubrics; the title reports a diocesan synod and chapter approval.
stages.witness_label: Missale Zagrabiense, Venetian print of 1511, OSZK RMK III 0176
stages.summary: The Usuarium catalogue identifies a 1511 missal according to Zagreb's choir and rubrics; its transcribed title reports confirmation and approval in a diocesan synod and general chapter under Bishop Luke. The contents inventory identifies the major Mass components.

evidence.locus: Book 92, Original title, Age, Printer and Shelfmark fields; Contents rows 3, 8, 281, 603–648
evidence.claim: The catalogue locates an exact 1511 print and transcribes the reported synod/chapter approval and Mass components.

stages.limitations: The transcribed title does not supply the original synod record, its date, legal reach, first use, or an exact comparison with medieval Zagreb manuscripts. No 1788 universal switch or parentage is inferred.
stages.reception: Diocesan destination and approval language are title-level attestations; actual use by a particular cathedral, parish or Jesuit house is not established here.

stages.label: 1690 Roman-Bohemian missal
stages.scope: Roman Missal book state whose long title advertises Bohemian saint Mass propers and pontifically conceded Masses under Archbishop Waldstein's mandate.
stages.summary: A 1690 digitized-book title identifies a Roman-based missal with Bohemian local Mass propers, including texts described as pontifically conceded, issued by command of Archbishop Johann Friedrich of Waldstein.

evidence.locus: Google Play Books listing, long title and imprint lines
evidence.claim: The title and imprint identify the 1690 Roman-Bohemian book and its stated local-proper and mandate scope.

stages.limitations: The original title and body, each concession, calendar, diocesan adoption and relation to the 1735 printing remain unchecked; the 1690 print is not made a descendant of the medieval Prague-use core.
stages.reception: A named archiepiscopal mandate on the title is not proof of reception at every Bohemian church or a first effective date.

gaps.missing: Direct collation of the 1519 print with earlier Nidaros Mass witnesses and province-by-province or parish use evidence.
gaps.next_source: Original 1519 print images and local inventories from Norway, Iceland and the Faroes; pre-1519 Nidaros ordo and missal fragments.
gaps.consequence: Publication is documented, but substantive predecessor changes and uniform provincial adoption cannot be dated.

gaps.missing: January, June and December calendar pages of the National Library composite are read; the Bitz preface leaf (not in pp. 1–24 of the composite), remaining calendar months, Mass components, other copies and actual Turku use dates remain.
gaps.next_source: Remaining pages of the acquired Doria composite PDF (pp. 25–540) for the preface woodcut leaf and Mass sections; Copenhagen parchment copy; paper copies listed by the National Library.
gaps.consequence: The diocesan book and local calendar are identified, but a full distinctive version and uptake cannot be reconstructed.

gaps.missing: The original synod and chapter act, source-text comparisons, exact diocesan reception and separate cathedral and Jesuit lines.
gaps.next_source: OSZK RMK III 0176 original book; Zagreb synod act; local directories and cathedral records.
gaps.consequence: The title's approval report cannot establish an act-history transition or a single later diocese-wide switch.

gaps.missing: Original printed title and propers, separate concession acts, local use and comparison with 1735 and medieval Prague materials.
gaps.next_source: National Library of the Czech Republic digitized 1690 copy and original archiepiscopal decree or approbation leaves.
gaps.consequence: The Roman-local book state is identifiable, but neither its exact prayer variants nor historical parentage is established.
